Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

her pronoun

belonging to her

also hers

classical

Gell. 1.23.7: animum ejus ad inquīrendum everberat

ejus

pronoun: genitive of is (feminine as masculine)

her (someone else’s)

When “her” is not the subject of the clause: the secret animum ejus … everberat, goads her mind. When it is the subject’s own, use suus (below). ejus does not show the owner’s sex: it is “his”, “her” or “its” alike.

Other words

  • suus, sua, suum — her (own), referring to the subject

    pronoun (possessive, reflexive), declension · classical · Cic. Att. 4.1.4: nātālī suō ipsō diē; Catull. 3.5: oculīs suīs

    As with “his”: it refers to the subject and agrees with the thing owned, nātālī suō, on her birthday.

  • illīus — her (that woman’s)

    pronoun: genitive of illa · also used · classical

    For a stronger or contrasting “her”.

Examples

  • mulier fit audiendī cupidior; sēcrētum reī et silentium puerī animum ejus ad inquīrendum everberat

    The woman grows more eager to hear; the secret and the boy’s silence goad her mind to find out.Gell. 1.23.7

  • ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē

    There my little Tullia was waiting for me, on her very birthday.Cic. Att. 4.1.4

  • passer mortuus est meae puellae, passer, dēliciae meae puellae, quem plūs illa oculīs suīs amābat

    My girl’s sparrow is dead, the sparrow, my girl’s darling, which she loved more than her own eyes.Catull. 3.3–5

  • ōrō tē … mulier, sine eam tōtam integram mātrem esse fīliī suī

    I beg you, madam, let her be wholly and entirely the mother of her own son.Gell. 12.1.5

See also she, his, its, their, own.
